narr: Thunderstorms developed across Surry County, NC ahead of a cold front sinking southward across Virginia during the afternoon and evening of July 18th. Deep instability was supported by surface temperatures warming into the upper 80s and low 90s, with surface-based CAPE values rising as high as 2,000 J/Kg by 4 pm. Deep moisture was observed pooling ahead of the cold front, with Precipitable Water values reaching an estimated 1.7 inches. Storms across the county showed signs of training across the same locations multiple times, while also producing 2 to 4 inch per hour rainfall rates.
ev: Doppler radar estimated that two to locally as much as four inches of rain from a series of thunderstorms fell across upper Moores Fork Creek basin (1.85 miles^2 per USGS Stream Stats), all within about a 2-hour period of time. For this duration, most locations within this area experienced between a 5- and a 10-year rainfall event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates. If indeed four inches of rain fell, that would be around a 100-year rainfall event at the 2-hour duration. Runoff from this rainfall caused Moores Fork Creek to rise out of its banks, flooding several inches deep across Kitty Hawk Lane and potentially other locations. No damage was reported.
